title: Attention Flows: Tracing LLM Conceptual Engagement via Story Summaries
abstract: arXiv:2604.06416v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Although LLM context lengths have grown, there is evidence that their ability to integrate information across long-form texts has not kept pace. We evaluate one such understanding task: generating summaries of novels. When human authors of summaries compress a story, they reveal what they consider narratively important. Therefore, by comparing human and LLM-authored summaries, we can assess whether models mirror human patterns of conceptual engagement with texts. To measure conceptual engagement, we align sentences from 150 human-written novel summaries with the specific chapters they reference. We demonstrate the difficulty of this alignment task, which indicates the complexity of summarization as a task. We then generate and align additional summaries by nine state-of-the-art LLMs for each of the 150 reference texts. translated_title: 注意力流动：通过故事摘要追踪LLM的概念参与度
translated_abstract: 尽管LLM的上下文长度已经增长，但有证据表明它们整合长文本信息的能力并未同步提升。我们评估了这样一种理解任务：生成小说摘要。当人类摘要作者压缩故事时，他们揭示了他们认为在叙事上重要的内容。因此，通过比较人类和LLM撰写的摘要，我们可以评估模型是否反映了人类与文本概念参与的模式。为了测量概念参与度，我们将150篇人类撰写的小说摘要中的句子与其引用的特定章节进行对齐。我们展示了这一对齐任务的难度，这说明了摘要作为一项任务的复杂性。然后，我们为每篇参考文本生成并对齐了由九种最先进的LLM撰写的额外摘要。比较人类和模型撰写的摘要，我们发现了文本之间的风格差异以及...
tldr: 该论文通过对比人类与LLM生成的小说摘要，评估模型在概念层面参与长文本的能力，并揭示了摘要任务中句子-章节对齐的复杂性及模型与人类在叙事重要性理解上的差异。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates LLMs' conceptual engagement with long texts by comparing human and model-authored novel summaries, highlighting the complexity of sentence-chapter alignment and differences in narrative importance.
